cards.front: What is the ir a + infinitive structure?
cards.back:
ir a + infinitive = going to do something (near future)

It expresses plans, intentions, and predictions about the future.

Voy a jugar píckleball. — I'm going to play pickleball.
Vamos a entrenar. — We're going to train.
Va a ganar. — He/she is going to win.
cards.grammarNote: This is the most common way to express future plans in conversational Spanish — more natural than the simple future tense.

cards.back:
yo voy
tú vas
él/ella/usted va
nosotros vamos
vosotros vais
ellos/ustedes van
cards.grammarNote: ir is completely irregular. Memorize these forms — they are the building block of ir a + infinitive.

cards.back:
[conjugated ir] + a + [infinitive]

yо voy a + correr → Voy a correr.
tú vas a + jugar → Vas a jugar.
él va a + ganar → Va a ganar.
nosotros vamos a + entrenar → Vamos a entrenar.
ellos van a + competir → Van a competir.
cards.grammarNote: The infinitive never changes, regardless of the subject. Only the form of ir is conjugated.

cards.front: Common sports plans with ir a
cards.back:
voy a jugar al píckleball — I'm going to play pickleball
vamos a entrenar — we're going to train
voy a hacer senderismo — I'm going to go hiking
voy a montar en bici — I'm going to ride my bike
voy a participar en el torneo — I'm going to enter the tournament
cards.grammarNote: ir a + infinitive is especially useful for talking about weekend plans and upcoming sports events.

cards.back:
Place no before the conjugated form of ir:

No voy a perder. — I'm not going to lose.
No vamos a llegar tarde. — We're not going to be late.
No va a llover hoy. — It's not going to rain today.
cards.grammarNote: The word 'no' goes before 'voy/vas/va…' — never between 'a' and the infinitive.

cards.front: ir a + infinitive with reflexive verbs
cards.back:
Two options — both are correct:

Voy a entrenARME. (pronoun attached to infinitive)
Me voy a entrenar. (pronoun before ir)

Voy a lesionarME → Me voy a lesionar.
Voy a calentarME → Me voy a calentar.
cards.grammarNote: With reflexive verbs, the reflexive pronoun can either attach to the infinitive or move to the front of the entire phrase.

cards.front: Time expressions used with ir a
cards.back:
esta tarde — this afternoon
esta noche — tonight
mañana — tomorrow
el fin de semana — the weekend
la próxima semana — next week
el sábado — on Saturday
pronto — soon
después — afterwards
cards.grammarNote: These time markers naturally pair with ir a + infinitive to specify when the future action will happen.

cards.front: Translate: Jeffrey is going to enter the tournament.
cards.back: Jeffrey va a participar en el torneo.
cards.grammarNote: va is the él/ella form of ir. participar en = to participate in / to enter (a competition).

cards.front: Translate: We are going to train every day this week.
cards.back: Vamos a entrenarnos todos los días esta semana.
cards.grammarNote: vamos a + infinitive for nosotros. 'todos los días' = every day; 'esta semana' = this week.

cards.front: Translate: I'm going to ride my bike to the park tomorrow.
cards.back: Mañana voy a montar en bici hasta el parque.
cards.grammarNote: Time adverbs like 'mañana' can start the sentence for emphasis. 'hasta el parque' = to/as far as the park.

cards.front: Translate: Are you going to stretch before the game?
cards.back:
¿Vas a estirarte antes del partido?
OR: ¿Te vas a estirar antes del partido?
cards.grammarNote: Both word orders for the reflexive pronoun are correct in questions. The rising intonation (question marks) signals the question.

cards.front: Translate: My brothers are going to come to the tournament.
cards.back: Mis hermanos van a venir al torneo.
cards.grammarNote: van is the ellos form of ir. venir (to come) is irregular but used here as the infinitive — it does not change.

cards.front: ir a for predictions (not just plans)
cards.back:
Va a ser un partido muy difícil.
(It's going to be a very difficult match.)

Van a ganar con facilidad.
(They're going to win easily.)

Vas a ser el campeón.
(You're going to be the champion.)
cards.grammarNote: ir a + infinitive is not limited to personal plans — it also expresses confident predictions about the future.

cards.front: ir a vs. the simple future tense
cards.back:
ir a + infinitive → conversational, near future, personal plans
Voy a jugar mañana. (I'm going to play tomorrow.)

Simple future (-é, -ás, -á…) → formal, distant future, predictions
Jugaré en el torneo nacional. (I will play in the national tournament.)
cards.grammarNote: In everyday speech, ir a + infinitive is far more common than the simple future. Use it for anything happening soon.

cards.front: Build a sentence: What are you going to do this Saturday?
cards.back:
¿Qué vas a hacer este sábado?

Possible answers:
Voy a jugar al píckleball con mis hermanos.
Voy a hacer senderismo en las montañas.
Voy a montar en bici y después voy a descansar.
cards.grammarNote: ¿Qué vas a hacer? is a very useful question pattern. Practice by replacing the infinitive with any activity.
